source.title: Driving the Wrong Way: Leveraging Interpretability in End2End Autonomous Driving Models

record.tranche_reason: Measures downstream driving performance with SAE reconstructions in an autonomous-driving model, bearing on whether SAE-based representations preserve model behavior; it does not analyze the structure of the reconstruction error.
record.gate_note: Table I reports downstream EPDMS scores for SAE-injected configurations, which are relevant to V5. The neuron zero-ablation results in Table II concern selected SAE features rather than the reconstruction error, so they are not recorded as rows for these claim versions. The study does not test error predictability, error scaling across SAE sizes, matched random errors, or the two proposed components of dark matter.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as an interpretability tool inside the GTRS driving model. Table I is a sweep for choosing the SAE configuration: reconstruction fidelity, ego metrics and EPDMS with the SAE spliced in. The error vector is never analysed. There is no linear prediction of the error, no scaling of error norms, no matched random-error control, and no comparison of circuits or steering with and without the error term. Their circuit and ablation analyses run on reconstructions with the error dropped, and they never measure what the error carries. So the EPDMS drop is a related downstream-fidelity measure for selecting their method, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim the SAE layer does not significantly alter predictive performance, and they treat Table I purely as a way to choose the parametrization. Zero-ablating neurons 177, 59 and 71 raises EPDMS from 0.4963 to 0.5926, above the original 0.524, while lowering ego progress.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates SAE reconstruction and downstream driving performance in GTRS; it does not use the original dark-matter error decomposition or test the error's linear predictability.
record.method_sensitivity: EPDMS varies with SAE architecture, neuron count, and k.

fits_no_version.finding: Splicing SAE reconstructions into GTRS's pre-scoring latent changes EPDMS from the original 0.524. Most TopK and Matryoshka configurations lower it modestly (0.418–0.51). Some match or exceed it (0.524, 0.552). Archetypal-style SAEs lower it sharply (0.151, 0.238).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Substituting SAE reconstructions for a vision/driving model's latent degrades downstream task performance by an amount that depends on SAE architecture and size, without a consistent monotone trend.

record.problems: The evidence on the claim is limited to EPDMS in the reported driving-model setting; no uncertainty estimates are given. The paper does not compare SAE reconstruction with matched random errors or test the reconstruction-error structure directly.
record.rows_left_out: Table II's combined zero-ablation result (including EPDMS 0.4963 baseline and 0.5926 ablated) is omitted because it tests selected-neuron interventions, not the SAE reconstruction error or its retention.

untested.parts: No regression of the SAE error on the input activations.
No per-token error norms, no cross-size prediction, and no overlap of failure contexts.
No matched random-error baseline for the EPDMS drop.
No split of the error into linear and nonlinear parts.
Circuits and ablations are run on reconstructions only. No comparison is made with the error term retained.
Architectures are compared on EPDMS and fidelity, but the error is never analysed as an artifact of training.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T2 verdict and its V5 labels are withdrawn. The study does not study reconstruction error and gives no uncertainty for the EPDMS values, so an above-baseline spliced score of 0.552 suggests the differences may partly be evaluation noise. R11's value was misread from the flattened table.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is linearly predictable from input activations.
Per-token error-norm prediction, overlap of failed contexts across SAE sizes, and whether error persists with scale.
No comparison with random errors of the same size.
No separation of linear and nonlinear error components or test of their learnability.
Tests aggregate driving-score performance with SAE reconstructions, not the effects of specifically retaining the error term in circuit analyses or steering.
Does not establish that reconstruction error is an artifact of training choices or test whether end-to-end training removes it.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The outcome depends on SAE configuration: R10 matches the original score, while R5 and R11 exceed it; EPDMS is an aggregate performance measure rather than a direct measure of circuits or steering behavior.
